narrativeReportMd:
# Device R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. `Device` keeps the same canonical identity, but R6 substantially reshapes local elements.

## Scope
This report covers local Device StructureDefinition changes and directly relevant local terminology/dependency evidence; inherited base-artifact changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
The largest themes are Reference→canonical conversion, stricter UDI carrier completeness, Device name/property reshaping, status availability semantics split, patient/owner movement to DeviceAssociation, and several path renames/removals.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `Device.definition`, `Device.udiCarrier`, `Device.name`, `Device.property`, `Device.status/statusReason`, and `Device.patient`/`owner`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for canonical resolution, name code mapping, property fan-out, status/availability mapping, DeviceAssociation creation, biological-source identifiers, conformance standards, and removed network URLs.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes are semantically reasonable but could have been staged with aliases, transitional choices, extensions, or official ConceptMaps.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze DeviceAssociation, DeviceDefinition, DeviceMetric/Observation, and Device search/profile behavior for complete migration planning.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 Device has multiple local hard breaks despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns are status semantics, moved patient/owner associations, and reshaped name/property/UDI/definition fields. Biggest uncertainty is lack of official cross-version mapping guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration requires data transformation, not just version relabeling: resolve DeviceDefinition canonicals, backfill UDI fields, rename/retype backbones, split associations into DeviceAssociation, and preserve R6-only codes/types through extensions or loss policies when converting back to R4.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because local StructureDefinitions and indexes were compared. Confidence is medium for exact migration intent and terminology edge cases because official diffs, full narrative migration guidance, and full terminology expansions were not available.

findings.title: Device.definition changed from Reference(DeviceDefinition) to canonical(DeviceDefinition)

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 serializes `definition` as a Reference object, while R6 expects a primitive canonical string. R6 versioned canonicals may not map back to an R4 Reference without resolving a concrete resource.

justification.inferredGoal: Identify the definitional DeviceDefinition by canonical URL rather than runtime Reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 Reference and add an optional canonical sibling for DeviceDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of identifying a definitional `DeviceDefinition` by canonical URL is reasonable and aligns with conformance-artifact practice. A less-breaking base design exists, but it is only partial because preserving the R4 `Reference` while adding a canonical would leave two ways to identify the same definition and would require precedence, validation, and resolution rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `Device.definition` as `Reference(DeviceDefinition)` for R4 compatibility and add an optional canonical element such as `definitionCanonical`, with clear deprecation and consistency guidance. This would preserve most R4 instances, but unresolved, contained, or identifier-only references still would not become canonical identifiers, and duplicate same-resource representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves existing Reference instances but creates duplicate link representations and conflict rules.

evidence.detail: R4 type is Reference targeting DeviceDefinition.
R6 type is canonical targeting DeviceDefinition.

findings.narrativeMd: `Device.definition` kept its path but changed datatype. Code using `definition.reference`, Reference search assumptions, or generated Reference classes must change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Reference object is not valid for an R6 canonical primitive. R6-to-R4 is lossy when a canonical includes a version or cannot be resolved as a resource Reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve R4 References to DeviceDefinition canonical URLs; flag contained, identifier-only, or unresolved references. For R6→R4, define an extension or reference-resolution policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transitional choice or sibling canonical element would have reduced breakage, but at the cost of two ways to link DeviceDefinition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 instances can carry `Device.definition` as a Reference object, while R6 expects a canonical string. That is a real validator and generated-model break, and versioned or unresolved canonicals can be lossy when converting back. Still, the field points to a definitional artifact, so moving to canonical identification is a coherent R6 design goal; retaining both Reference and canonical forms in the base resource would create precedence and consistency problems.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Device.definition: 0..1 Reference(DeviceDefinition)
R6 StructureDefinition Device.definition: 0..1 canonical(DeviceDefinition)
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral under the framework: it does not create a normative stability burden, but it also does not erase the concrete path-level break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a valid R4 Reference object at `definition` is not valid against the R6 canonical primitive; R6-to-R4 may also require resolving a canonical to a concrete reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep the Reference and add a canonical sibling, but that would leave two authoritative ways to identify the same DeviceDefinition and require conflict rules. That tradeoff makes the break proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a hard/high break with only a partial less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: UDI carrier repetitions now require deviceIdentifier and issuer

oldState.summary: In R4, `udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier` and `udiCarrier.issuer` are each optional (`0..1`).
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier` and `udiCarrier.issuer` are each optional (`0..1`).

newState.summary: In R6, a present `udiCarrier` must contain `deviceIdentifier` and `issuer` (`1..1` each); `deviceIdentifierSystem` is added optional.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, a present `udiCarrier` must contain `deviceIdentifier` and `issuer` (`1..1` each); `deviceIdentifierSystem` is added optional.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 UDI carrier with only HRF/AIDC or metadata becomes invalid in R6. R6 adds deviceIdentifierSystem, which is not representable in R4 base.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure UDI carrier repetitions have the mandatory DI and issuing organization.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `deviceIdentifier` and `issuer` optional in base and enforce completeness through warnings or profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring the DI and issuer on each UDI carrier is a strong traceability and safety goal. The break is material for partial historical UDI captures, but a fully backward-compatible base alternative would not ensure the same level of completeness across all conformant R6 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could leave `udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier` and `udiCarrier.issuer` at `0..1`, add `deviceIdentifierSystem`, and use a best-practice invariant, warning, or profile to require complete UDI data where needed. That preserves old partial carrier strings, but it only partially meets the R6 goal because base-valid instances could still omit the core DI and issuer.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves partial historical scans but weakens the base guarantee needed for UDI traceability.

evidence.detail: Both child minimum cardinalities are 0 in R4.
Both child minimum cardinalities are 1 in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes partial UDI carrier data invalid. Systems that only scanned carrier strings must derive or backfill DI and issuer.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs when `udiCarrier` is present without both required children. Devices with no UDI carrier are unaffected.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Parse DI and issuer from HRF/AIDC where possible; otherwise quarantine, backfill, or preserve partial data with an extension and data-quality flag.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Profiles or warning invariants could have preserved partial base data while encouraging complete UDI capture.

freshReview.narrativeMd: A partial R4 UDI carrier, such as one that only stores the scanned HRF/AIDC string, no longer satisfies base R6 because each carrier must include both the device identifier and issuer. That can require parsing or data cleanup, but the required fields are the core traceability components of a UDI. For a safety- and regulatory-relevant identifier, making the base model guarantee those parts is a reasonable burden.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier and Device.udiCarrier.issuer: min 0
R6 Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier and Device.udiCarrier.issuer: min 1
R6 adds Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifierSystem as optional namespace support
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral; the judgment is driven by the concrete old-valid/new-invalid mechanism and the safety/regulatory traceability value of complete UDI data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `udiCarrier` repetition without `deviceIdentifier` or without `issuer` is rejected by R6; R6 `deviceIdentifierSystem` also has no R4 base field.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the two children optional and used warnings or profiles for completeness. That would preserve partial historical scans, but it would fail the base-level guarantee that each UDI carrier is traceable to a DI and issuing agency.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high impact and partial-alternative assessment matches the fresh path-level review.

findings.title: Device.deviceName was reshaped to Device.name with changed child names and terminology

oldState.summary: R4 `deviceName` is repeating; child `name` is string and child `type` is a required-bound primitive code.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `deviceName` is repeating; child `name` is string and child `type` is a required-bound primitive code.

newState.summary: R6 `name` is repeating; child `value` is string, child `type` is CodeableConcept with extensible binding, optional `display`, and root invariant `dev-1` limiting display=true to one name.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `name` is repeating; child `value` is string, child `type` is CodeableConcept with extensible binding, optional `display`, and root invariant `dev-1` limiting display=true to one name.

facts.field: R4 codes absent from R6 code system

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions and child structure show `deviceName` corresponds to R6 `name`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON uses an element name R6 does not define, and the type child changes from primitive enum-like code to CodeableConcept. R6 names can carry codings/display flags that R4 cannot represent cleanly.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize device names and identify a preferred display name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `deviceName`/`name` with old codes while adding preferred-display support and richer typing.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of richer device-name modeling and a preferred display name is reasonable. The rename and primitive-code to `CodeableConcept` change are disruptive, but avoiding them completely would either give up part of the richer terminology model or add parallel old and new name-type fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep the R4 `deviceName.name` and `deviceName.type` shape, retain the R4 codes alongside the R6 codes, and add an optional display flag. That would cover many cases and preserve R4 instances, but it would not fully support the R6 `CodeableConcept` model unless a duplicative richer type field was added, creating long-term mapping and conflict risk.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 names but either limits CodeableConcept expressiveness or duplicates name-type representations.

evidence.detail: R4 uses `deviceName.name` and primitive `deviceName.type` with required binding.
R6 uses `name.value`, CodeableConcept `name.type`, optional `display`, and invariant dev-1.
R4 and R6 DeviceNameType code systems differ materially.

examples.examplesMd: Mapping manufacturer-name to registered-name is jurisdiction-sensitive.

findings.narrativeMd: The name backbone rename is a validation break and a generated-model break. The terminology change is nuanced: binding strength relaxes, but several R4 codes disappeared from the local R6 code system.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `deviceName` content is invalid in R6 until renamed. R6 CodeableConcept name types and display metadata are not cleanly representable in R4 primitive `type`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `deviceName` to `name`, move `name` to `value`, convert primitive codes to CodeableConcept, map removed codes with human-reviewed rules, and set at most one `display=true`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias or transition period could have preserved old data but would create duplicate name representations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is more than a cosmetic rename. R4 uses `deviceName.name` plus a required primitive name-type code; R6 uses `name.value`, a CodeableConcept type with an extensible binding, a preferred-display flag, and an invariant limiting display names. Common R4 name records will not validate until transformed, and several R4 name-type codes do not exist in the R6 complete code system. The richer model is useful, but the old wire names could plausibly have been retained while adding richer typing or display metadata.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.deviceName.name: required string; Device.deviceName.type: required code bound to R4 device-nametype
R6 Device.name.value: required string; Device.name.type: required CodeableConcept; Device.name.display: optional boolean
R6 Device root invariant dev-1 limits `name.where(display=true).count()` to one
R4 device-nametype includes udi-label-name, manufacturer-name, model-name, other; R6 device-nametype includes registered-name, user-friendly-name, patient-reported-name
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral, but device names are a plausible common display/search field, so the avoidable wire-format churn carries real migration cost even without mature/normative stability pressure.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `deviceName` and `deviceName.name` are not R6 element names, and R4 primitive codes require conversion to an R6 CodeableConcept and possibly new code semantics.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep `deviceName.name` as the wire shape, add an optional display flag, and either retain old name-type codes or introduce a richer optional type representation. That would have some duplicate-type risk, but simply preserving the old path names looks relatively low cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a high hard break, but the fresh review gives more weight to the avoidability of the path rename and code churn.

findings.title: Device.property values changed from two repeating value elements to one required choice

oldState.summary: R4 property has optional repeating `valueQuantity` and optional repeating `valueCode`; a property can have no values or multiple values.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 property has optional repeating `valueQuantity` and optional repeating `valueCode`; a property can have no values or multiple values.

newState.summary: R6 property has required single `value[x]` with Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, or Attachment.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 property has required single `value[x]` with Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, or Attachment.

facts.newValue: static/fixed characteristics; dynamic settings use DeviceMetric/Observation

impact.impactRationaleMd: Empty R4 property repetitions become invalid; old multi-valued properties require fan-out; new R6 choice types cannot be represented in R4 base.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize property values and broaden allowed value types while clarifying static-versus-dynamic property semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional repeating `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` while adding staged support for the new `value[x]` types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing each property repetition to one required value and broadening value types is a coherent R6 modeling goal. A less-breaking design exists, but it would only partially meet that goal because it would keep the old ability to represent empty or multi-valued property repetitions in base Device.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A staged base design could retain the R4 `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` repetitions, add the new scalar/range/attachment value choices, and use warnings or profiles to encourage one value per property. This would preserve R4 instances but would create validation ambiguity about which representation is authoritative and would delay cleanup of dynamic-setting content that R6 directs to DeviceMetric or Observation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old sparse and multi-valued properties but prolongs ambiguous duplicate property-value modeling.

evidence.detail: R4 has two optional repeating value elements.
R6 has one required choice value per property.

examples.examplesMd: Multi-valued R4 properties need policy-driven fan-out.

findings.narrativeMd: `Device.property` is a major content-model and JSON-name change: `valueCode` becomes `valueCodeableConcept`, one value is required, and multiple values need multiple property repetitions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs for property entries without a value or with R4 value element names. R6 strings/booleans/integers/ranges/attachments are R6-valid but not R4-representable without extensions or lossy text.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename value elements, reject or enrich empty properties, fan out multi-valued properties, and consider DeviceMetric/Observation for dynamic settings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transitional optional `value[x]` plus deprecated old fields would have reduced migration breaks but prolonged ambiguous modeling.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a property entry with zero or many `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` repetitions. R6 requires exactly one `value[x]` per property, changes the CodeableConcept JSON name, adds more datatypes, and narrows the prose toward static characteristics while directing dynamic observations elsewhere. That is substantial migration work, but the normalized one-property-one-value model is clearer and the less-breaking options would preserve ambiguous empty and multi-valued property entries.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.property.valueQuantity: 0..* Quantity
R4 Device.property.valueCode: 0..* CodeableConcept
R6 Device.property.value[x]: 1..1 with Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Attachment
R6 Device.property definition/comment distinguish static characteristics from dynamic DeviceMetric/Observation data
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral. It keeps this from being a normative-stability concern, while the concrete instance and mapper break still matter.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: empty R4 property repetitions and R4 `valueCode`/multi-value shapes are not valid as R6 `value[x]`; new R6 value types are lossy to base R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the old optional repeating value fields and added new choices, or made the new choice optional during transition. That would preserve more R4 data but keep duplicate/ambiguous representations and weaken the R6 normalization goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high impact and partial-alternative framing is consistent with the fresh review, even though the final judgment treats the break as proportionate.

findings.title: Device.status changed from availability semantics to record status and statusReason was removed

oldState.summary: R4 `Device.status` means availability; `statusReason` carries operational/availability reasons such as online, offline, standby, hardware disconnected, and off.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `Device.status` means availability; `statusReason` carries operational/availability reasons such as online, offline, standby, hardware disconnected, and off.

newState.summary: R6 `Device.status` means record status, explicitly not device availability; `statusReason` is removed and R6 adds `availabilityStatus` plus DeviceAssociation status/relationship fields.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Device.status` means record status, explicitly not device availability; `statusReason` is removed and R6 adds `availabilityStatus` plus DeviceAssociation status/relationship fields.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `statusReason` removal is a hard validation break. More dangerously, copied `status` codes can still validate but mean record lifecycle instead of physical availability.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate record lifecycle from device availability and association/operational state.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 `status`/`statusReason` for availability and add a new `recordStatus` element for lifecycle state.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating record lifecycle from device availability is reasonable, but reusing `Device.status` with the same codes and a different meaning creates avoidable semantic risk. A base R6 design could have met the separation goal while preserving old availability data and making the new lifecycle meaning explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would leave R4 `Device.status` and `Device.statusReason` as deprecated availability fields and add a distinct `recordStatus` for the R6 record-lifecycle concept. This preserves R4-valid instances and avoids silent `active`/`inactive` semantic drift. The tradeoff is an extra status-like element and a longer transition away from the imperfect old `status` name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another status-like field but avoids silent reinterpretation of existing `status` codes.

evidence.detail: R4 definition: Status of the Device availability.
R6 definition: Device record status, not availability.
R4 has statusReason; R6 Device does not.
R6 DeviceAssociation carries relationship and association status concepts.

examples.examplesMd: Offline/standby may map to DeviceAssociation rather than availabilityStatus.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a high-risk semantic break because `active`/`inactive` may validate in both versions while changing business meaning. Old `statusReason` data has no same-path R6 target.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `statusReason` are invalid in R6. R4 instances with only `status` may validate but can be semantically wrong unless transformed to record status, availabilityStatus, or DeviceAssociation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not copy status blindly. Classify old values as record lifecycle, availability, association, or operational state; populate R6 Device.status, Device.availabilityStatus, and/or DeviceAssociation accordingly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new `recordStatus` element with deprecated old availability status would have avoided silent semantic drift but added another status field.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This change is risky because the same `active` and `inactive` codes can continue to validate while their meaning changes from physical availability/implantation state to record lifecycle. R4 `statusReason` is also removed, and the R6 availability replacement uses a different field and different code set. A migration that copies status mechanically can silently corrupt business or clinical interpretation.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.status definition: status of device availability; R4 device-status active means available/implanted
R6 Device.status definition: record status, explicitly not availability
R4 Device.statusReason exists as 0..* CodeableConcept; R6 Device.statusReason is absent
R6 Device.availabilityStatus exists as 0..1 CodeableConcept with availability codes such as lost, damaged, destroyed, available
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral, but status is a central modifier-like workflow field and the semantic drift is safety/business relevant, so FMM does not soften the concern enough to accept the design.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the highest-risk mechanism is same-code semantic drift; additionally, R4 instances with `statusReason` are old-valid/new-invalid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could have kept `Device.status` and `statusReason` for availability, marked them deprecated if needed, and added a distinct `recordStatus` for lifecycle. That would add another status field but avoid silent reinterpretation of existing codes.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report identifies this as a high-impact hard and semantic break with a plausible less-breaking design.

findings.title: Device.patient and Device.owner were removed and moved to DeviceAssociation-style associations

oldState.summary: R4 Device directly carries optional `patient` Reference(Patient) and `owner` Reference(Organization).
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Device directly carries optional `patient` Reference(Patient) and `owner` Reference(Organization).

newState.summary: R6 Device has no `patient` or `owner`; DeviceAssociation links a device to subjects/foci with relationship codes including patient and owner.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Device has no `patient` or `owner`; DeviceAssociation links a device to subjects/foci with relationship codes including patient and owner.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: DeviceAssociation is the R6 local resource whose definitions and relationship codes cover patient/owner associations.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 inline patient/owner references are invalid in R6 Device. Migration changes resource boundaries and may require new DeviceAssociation resources with required status.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent time-varying device relationships as first-class association resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated inline `patient` and `owner` for simple current associations while adding DeviceAssociation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving relationships to `DeviceAssociation` supports multiple, typed, perioded, and statused associations. Keeping the R4 inline fields would reduce migration pain, but it would be an incomplete alternative because it cannot represent the richer relationship lifecycle and would create consistency ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `Device.patient` and `Device.owner` as deprecated shortcuts for the current patient and owner while adding `DeviceAssociation` as the authoritative model for richer relationships. This preserves common R4 instances, but it risks conflicting inline and association resources, complicates search, and does not handle multiple or time-varying associations without the new resource.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Covers common R4 cases but duplicates association sources and cannot express the full DeviceAssociation model.

evidence.detail: R4 has direct patient and owner references.
R6 Device has no patient or owner elements.
DeviceAssociation supports device relationships including patient and owner.

examples.examplesMd: Owner likely needs a separate DeviceAssociation.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 patient/owner data must move out of Device. This affects validation, persistence, transactions, search, and client code that assumed association data was inline.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `patient`/`owner` fields are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 DeviceAssociation can represent multiple, perioded, statused associations that cannot fully collapse into R4 single fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create DeviceAssociation resources with relationship `patient` or `owner`, populate required status, and update clients/searches to query associations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping deprecated inline fields during transition would have reduced breakage but risked conflicting association sources.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 lets the Device directly identify the patient it is associated with and the owning organization. R6 removes those inline fields and expects relationship data to live in DeviceAssociation, which changes resource boundaries, transactions, queries, and client models. DeviceAssociation is a stronger model for multiple and time-varying relationships, but the base spec could plausibly have retained deprecated inline shortcuts for the simple current patient/owner cases while introducing the association resource.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.patient: 0..1 Reference(Patient)
R4 Device.owner: 0..1 Reference(Organization)
R6 Device has no patient or owner elements
R6 DeviceAssociation.device is required, subject can reference Patient or Organization, relationship includes patient and owner codes, and status is required
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral, but patient/device association is clinically and operationally important enough that a resource-boundary move deserves heightened scrutiny.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `patient` and `owner` properties are rejected on R6 Device; migration requires creating separate DeviceAssociation resources and updating APIs/searches.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping deprecated inline `patient` and `owner` while adding DeviceAssociation would preserve many R4 instances and simple reads. The tradeoff is duplicate sources of truth and harder consistency/search rules, but that may be preferable for a staged transition.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly sees a high hard break and a partial alternative, but the fresh review judges the resource-boundary migration as important enough to revisit.

findings.title: Device.version was renamed to Device.deviceVersion and gained installDate

oldState.summary: R4 `Device.version` is a repeating backbone with `type`, `component`, and required `value`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `Device.version` is a repeating backbone with `type`, `component`, and required `value`.

newState.summary: R6 `Device.deviceVersion` is the corresponding repeating backbone and adds optional `installDate`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Device.deviceVersion` is the corresponding repeating backbone and adds optional `installDate`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Parallel definitions and child structure show a rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The shared content maps cleanly, but the JSON key changed. R6 installDate has no R4 base destination.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that this is the device/software version, not the FHIR resource version.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `Device.version` backbone, clarify its definition, and add optional `installDate` there.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that the field is a device or software version is reasonable, but the path rename was not necessary to achieve that goal. The same content model could have been preserved with clearer definitions and an additive optional child.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design would retain `Device.version` with its existing `type`, `component`, and `value` children, add optional `version.installDate`, and update definitions to distinguish it from resource metadata versioning. The main cost is continuing to live with the less explicit R4 name, which is a modest tradeoff compared with invalidating existing instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains a potentially confusing old name but avoids a wire rename and duplicate version backbones.

evidence.detail: R4 has Device.version.
R6 has Device.deviceVersion plus installDate.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a straightforward path rename with a small R6-only addition, but it still breaks validators and generated models.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `version` is invalid in R6 until renamed. R6 `deviceVersion.installDate` is not representable in R4 without extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `version` to `deviceVersion` and copy `type`, `component`, and `value`; preserve installDate in an extension for R6→R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias would have avoided a hard break with modest complexity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The shared content of the version backbone maps cleanly, but the wire name changed from `version` to `deviceVersion`. The likely goal is to avoid confusion with resource metadata versions, yet that goal could be met by clarifying the existing element definition and adding the optional install date without invalidating existing payloads.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.version: 0..* backbone with required value
R6 Device.deviceVersion: 0..* backbone with required value
R6 Device.deviceVersion.installDate added as optional dateTime
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral; because this appears primarily to be a naming cleanup, the absence of mature status does not make the hard rename cost disappear.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `version` array is not an R6 `deviceVersion` array; generated models and persistence columns also change names.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: The base spec could have retained `Device.version`, clarified that it is the device/software version, and added `version.installDate`. That is a low-cost alternative whose main drawback is preserving a less explicit element name.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing medium impact and yes-alternative assessment align with this being an avoidable hard rename.

findings.title: Device.specialization was replaced by Device.conformsTo

oldState.summary: R4 `specialization` has required `systemType` CodeableConcept and optional `version`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `specialization` has required `systemType` CodeableConcept and optional `version`.

newState.summary: R6 `conformsTo` has required `specification` CodeableConcept, optional `category`, and optional `version`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `conformsTo` has required `specification` CodeableConcept, optional `category`, and optional `version`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both describe standards/specifications supported by the device.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `specialization` is invalid in R6. R6 `category` has no R4 destination and code mapping may need review.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize device specialization/capability standards into standards/specifications/formal guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `specialization.systemType` with clearer conformance wording and add optional `category`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing standards and formal guidance is reasonable, but the R4 backbone already carried standards conformance information. Renaming both the backbone and required child appears avoidable because clearer definitions and an additive category could provide most of the R6 semantics on the old shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design would keep `Device.specialization.systemType` and `Device.specialization.version`, broaden the definitions to cover standards, specifications, and formal guidance, and add optional `specialization.category`. That preserves R4 instances and avoids same-resource duplication. The tradeoff is retaining the less precise `specialization` and `systemType` names.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Old naming is less clear, but the goal can be met without duplicate representations or invalidating R4 content.

evidence.detail: R4 specialization has systemType and version.
R6 conformsTo has specification, category, and version.

examples.examplesMd: Category may be lost in R6→R4.

findings.narrativeMd: The conformance-standard backbone was renamed and broadened. It is likely mappable, but not by simple copy.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `specialization` is invalid in R6. R6 `conformsTo.category` is R6-valid/not-R4-representable in base Device.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `specialization.systemType` to `conformsTo.specification`, copy version, and infer category only with reliable rules.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias or official ConceptMap would have reduced ambiguity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `specialization.systemType` and R6 `conformsTo.specification` both describe standards or specifications the device supports. R6 broadens the wording and adds category, but the base model could have kept the old backbone and child names while broadening definitions and adding an optional category. The rename invalidates existing content for a relatively modest terminology/modeling cleanup.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.specialization: 0..* backbone; systemType is required CodeableConcept; version is optional
R6 Device.conformsTo: 0..* backbone; specification is required CodeableConcept; category and version are optional
R6 conformsTo definition covers standards, specifications, formal guidances, certification, and related capabilities
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral. The field may be less common, but standards/protocol conformance can affect interoperability workflows, and the rename has a plausible lower-cost alternative.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `specialization` and `systemType` are not valid R6 paths; R6 `category` has no R4 base destination.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could retain `specialization.systemType`, update its definitions to include formal guidance and certifications, and add `specialization.category`. That preserves old instances with little ambiguity beyond living with older names.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's medium impact and yes-alternative judgment fit the fresh assessment.

findings.title: Device.distinctIdentifier was removed; biological traceability is now biologicalSourceEvent

oldState.summary: R4 `distinctIdentifier` is `0..1 string` for a regulatory distinct identification string for human cell/tissue products.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `distinctIdentifier` is `0..1 string` for a regulatory distinct identification string for human cell/tissue products.

newState.summary: R6 `biologicalSourceEvent` is `0..1 Identifier` for the donor, donation, or pooling event associated with biological material.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `biologicalSourceEvent` is `0..1 Identifier` for the donor, donation, or pooling event associated with biological material.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions/mappings point to related biological traceability concepts but datatype and semantics differ.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 string data is invalid in R6 and must be structured as Identifier. R6 Identifier system/type metadata is lossy when collapsed to R4 string.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve biological-source traceability with a structured event identifier.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `distinctIdentifier` string while adding structured `biologicalSourceEvent` Identifier.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of structured biological-source traceability is strong, especially for safety and regulatory use. A compatibility path exists, but it is partial because the R4 string cannot carry Identifier system, type, and event semantics without either loss or a second field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could retain `Device.distinctIdentifier` as a deprecated string and add `Device.biologicalSourceEvent` as the structured Identifier. This preserves R4 instances, but old strings may not reliably identify the same biological source event, and maintaining both fields creates reconciliation and safety risks when values diverge.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old regulatory strings but duplicates traceability data or loses Identifier metadata.

evidence.detail: R4 has optional string distinctIdentifier.
R6 has optional Identifier biologicalSourceEvent.

examples.examplesMd: Identifier system should be supplied when known.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not a simple string rename; the target is an Identifier with event semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `distinctIdentifier` is invalid in R6. R6 `biologicalSourceEvent.system` and other Identifier metadata cannot be represented in R4 string without loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old strings to `biologicalSourceEvent.value` only when they identify the source event; populate Identifier.system where known and review ambiguous values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping the old string as deprecated would have eased migration but duplicated traceability fields.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 used a plain string for a regulated distinct identifier on human cell, tissue, or cellular/tissue-based products. R6 replaces that with an Identifier for the biological source event, with comments emphasizing donor/source-to-recipient traceability and anonymity. That invalidates old strings and can require expert mapping, but the target model is meaningfully more computable for a safety- and regulatory-relevant traceability concept.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.distinctIdentifier: 0..1 string for a regulatory distinct identification string
R6 Device.biologicalSourceEvent: 0..1 Identifier for donor, donation, or pooling event
R6 comment states the element supports mandatory traceability from donor/source to recipient while satisfying donor anonymity
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral, but the domain is safety/regulatory traceability; that supports accepting a structured replacement despite the trial-use maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 string at `distinctIdentifier` is not valid in R6; R6 Identifier metadata such as system/type cannot be represented in the R4 string without loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained a deprecated `distinctIdentifier` string and added `biologicalSourceEvent`. That would ease migration, but it risks two divergent identifiers for safety-critical traceability and does not ensure the old string actually identifies the source event.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing medium impact and partial-alternative assessment is consistent with treating the break as real but proportionate.

findings.title: Device.url was removed with no same-path R6 replacement

oldState.summary: R4 `Device.url` is `0..1 uri` for a network address on which the device may be contacted directly.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `Device.url` is `0..1 uri` for a network address on which the device may be contacted directly.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data using Device as a direct network endpoint registry becomes invalid in R6. No local Device replacement was found.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly remove direct network endpoint contact from Device.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `Device.url` as deprecated with guidance to use the appropriate endpoint or communication model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local evidence shows removal but no same-path replacement or clear rationale. If the goal was to discourage direct network endpoints on Device, deprecating and documenting the old optional field would have been a less-breaking way to stage that goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could retain `Device.url` at `0..1 uri`, mark it deprecated or narrowly scoped, and point implementers to the intended R6 communication or endpoint model when available. This avoids invalidating existing endpoint URLs. The tradeoff is continued support for a field that may be stale or modelled better elsewhere.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves a possibly stale direct network-address field, but preserves R4 data with little base-model complexity.

evidence.detail: R4 has Device.url.
R6 Device has no Device.url.

examples.examplesMd: No local R6 Device replacement was identifiable.

findings.narrativeMd: `Device.url` removal is a hard validation break for devices that carried direct network contact URLs.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `url` are invalid in R6. There is no R6-to-R4 issue for this path because R6 has no local replacement field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `Device.url` use and identify the appropriate R6 endpoint/communication model or use a governed extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated element or official extension would have preserved old endpoint data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Device.url` carried a direct network address, including a possible FHIR server base URL for the device. R6 removes the field and the local evidence did not show a same-path replacement. Because it was optional and could have been deprecated with guidance toward the intended endpoint/communication model, outright deletion looks more breaking than necessary.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.url: 0..1 uri, defined as a network address on which the device may be contacted directly
R4 Device.url comment mentions a device FHIR server base URL
R6 Device snapshot has no Device.url element
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral. The path may be rare, but the lack of a clear replacement and the low cost of keeping an optional deprecated field support revisiting the deletion.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Device with `url` is invalid against the R6 Device StructureDefinition, with no local R6 Device field to receive the value.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep `Device.url` optional and mark it deprecated or narrowly scoped while documenting the preferred endpoint model. The tradeoff is carrying a potentially stale direct-address field for one more transition.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's medium impact and yes-alternative assessment match the fresh review.

findings.title: Device.type widened from 0..1 to 0..*

newState.summary: R6 `Device.type` is optional repeating CodeableConcept (`0..*`) for devices with multiple classifications.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Device.type` is optional repeating CodeableConcept (`0..*`) for devices with multiple classifications.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances remain valid in R6, but R6 instances with multiple types break R4 scalar models and cannot round-trip without loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow devices to have multiple applicable types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed for this R6 expansion.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple device classifications is a reasonable R6 goal. As assessed here, the change widens the R6 content model rather than removing or narrowing R4 semantic content, so the backward-compatible-alternative question is not the right frame.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This finding is primarily a down-conversion and generated-model concern. R6 instances with multiple `type` values need a policy for R4 conversion, such as choosing a primary type and preserving extras elsewhere, but that is a migration mitigation rather than a less-breaking base R6 design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The compatibility issue is R6-to-R4 loss when multiple types are used, not rejection of R4 type content by the R6 model.

evidence.detail: R4 max is 1.
R6 max is *.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry only one type.

findings.narrativeMd: This is sender-compatible R4→R6 but a real R6→R4 and code-generation risk for scalar APIs and databases.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No old-valid/new-invalid case exists. R6-valid multiple `type` values are not representable in R4 base Device without choosing one or using extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update models and schemas to treat `type` as repeating. For R6→R4 choose a primary type and preserve extras in extensions if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Extensions could have preserved scalar compatibility but would make multiple classifications less interoperable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `Device.type` from a single CodeableConcept to a repeating one. Existing R4 instances with zero or one type remain representable by R6, and the migration is normally just wrapping the old value in an array/list-aware model. The only real issue is reverse conversion or scalar application code encountering multiple R6 types.
keyEvidence: R4 Device.type: 0..1 CodeableConcept
R6 Device.type: 0..* CodeableConcept
R6 comment explains multiple types for devices categorized in more than one context
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral, and because this is an R4-to-R6 widening rather than a rejection of old content, maturity does not create a reason to revisit the design.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: multiple R6 type values cannot fit into base R4 without choosing one or using extensions; R4-to-R6 instance validation is not broken.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Keeping the max at 1 would preserve scalar models but fail the stated multi-classification use case.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report is right about reverse loss and no applicable less-breaking alternative, but its medium impact overstates the R4-to-R6 concern.

findings.title: UDI entryType required value set added electronic-transmission

oldState.summary: R4 required UDIEntryType codes do not include `electronic-transmission`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required UDIEntryType codes do not include `electronic-transmission`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old R4 codes remain acceptable in R6, but R4 validators/enums reject the new R6 required-bound code.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent UDI received electronically through a communication protocol.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because old required-bound codes are retained.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `electronic-transmission` captures a distinct UDI capture method that is not precisely represented by the R4 codes. Because R4 codes remain valid in R6, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using an old R4 code such as `unknown` for electronically transmitted UDI data would lose information, and an extension-only representation would make the new concept less interoperable. The remaining problem is down-conversion to R4 systems, which requires a lossy mapping or extension policy rather than a backward-compatible R6 base alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The new code creates R6-to-R4 enum/validation loss, but does not invalidate R4 instances in R6.

evidence.detail: R4 local complete CodeSystem lacks electronic-transmission.
R6 local complete CodeSystem includes electronic-transmission.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a directional enum break for R4 receivers of R6 data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4→R6 break for retained codes. R6→R4 validation breaks when `entryType` is `electronic-transmission` under a required binding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update enum handling. For R6→R4, reject, map to `unknown`, or preserve original code in an extension; `unknown` loses information.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The addition is justified because no R4 code precisely conveys electronic transmission.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds `electronic-transmission` to the required UDI entry type code system while retaining the R4 codes. That does not invalidate R4 instances moving to R6. R4 receivers of R6 data may reject the new code, but that is a reverse-version interoperability issue and the new code captures a distinct capture mechanism that would be lossy if forced into an older value.
keyEvidence: R4 CodeSystem udi-entry-type lacks electronic-transmission and includes barcode, rfid, manual, card, self-reported, unknown
R6 CodeSystem udi-entry-type adds electronic-transmission and retains the R4 codes
R6 definition: UDI information received electronically from the device through a communication protocol such as IEEE 11073 over Bluetooth or USB
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 is neutral; since this is additive for R4-to-R6 and not a base rejection of old data, maturity does not increase concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 `entryType` of `electronic-transmission` is outside the R4 required value set; old R4 codes remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed. Mapping electronic transmission to `unknown` or using only an extension would be less interoperable and less precise.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly marks the alternative as not applicable, but its medium impact is too high for an additive R4-to-R6 terminology change.
